src: research-tools/build_vsa_explanations.py (paraphrased from the library: MTM, Holmes, WTW, Holmes SEQ; VSA_METHOD.md §4; vsa_config.json matrix)

SC.name: Selling climax
SC.what: A wide down bar into new lows after a decline, on ultra-high volume, closing well off its low.
SC.pro: The crowd is panic-selling and professional money is buying everything offered; that buying is why the bar closes off its low.
SC.next: Expect the climax area to be tested on low volume. A quiet test or no-supply bar confirms the buying; heavy selling back through the low cancels it.

SV.name: Stopping volume
SV.what: Heavy volume on a down bar during a reaction, closing in the upper half of its range.
SV.pro: Professional money is stepping in to stop the fall and soak up the selling. Its meaning depends on the background: with buying behind it, bullish; in a downtrend with weakness behind it, often only a pause.
SV.next: The next bar should be up. Then look for a low-volume test of the area before prices can rise properly.
SV.ref: MTM p.97, p.168; Holmes p.101-102; WTW v2 p.68

BAG.name: Bag holding
BAG.what: A narrow down bar on ultra-high volume after a fall, closing in the middle or higher.
BAG.pro: Professionals are holding out the bag: taking every share the panicking crowd sells, which is why the spread stays narrow despite the volume.
BAG.next: Rare and usually strong, especially into new lows. Look for the next bar to rise and for later tests to hold above the bag-holding low.
BAG.ref: MTM p.142; Holmes p.100; WTW v2 p.16

SO.name: Shakeout
SO.what: A wide bar marked down below recent lows that closes near its high.
SO.pro: A deliberate mark-down to trigger stops and scare weak holders out; the selling is absorbed and prices are marked straight back up.
SO.next: Look for a low-volume test of the shakeout area. If the shakeout came on very heavy volume, that supply may need testing before a rally.

T.name: Test
T.what: A bar that dips under the prior low but closes high, on a narrow spread and low volume.
T.pro: Professional money marks prices down to see whether any sellers are left. Low volume says supply has dried up, so they can mark prices up with less resistance.
T.next: An up bar next confirms the test. No response after a test, or a new low on heavy volume, is weakness.

TR.name: Test in a rising market
TR.what: In an uptrend: a narrow down bar closing on its low on very low volume, inside the prior bar's range.
TR.pro: A quiet dip that finds no sellers: professionals are content to keep holding and are not supplying stock.
TR.next: A higher close on the next bar confirms it. It works best near the bottom of the uptrend channel.

NS.name: No supply
NS.what: A narrow down bar on volume lower than each of the two previous bars.
NS.pro: Professional money isn't selling into the dip, so there is little supply.
NS.next: The next bar should close up to confirm it. It matters most with strength in the background; in a downtrend it may bring only a pause or a small bounce.

ETR.name: Effort to rise
ETR.what: A wide up bar closing near its high on increased volume.
ETR.pro: Genuine buying effort: professionals are marking prices up and demand is beating supply.
ETR.next: Healthy if later pullbacks come on low volume. If the next bars fail to follow through, or huge volume makes little progress, supply is present.

ABS.name: Absorption volume
ABS.what: Heavy volume with little price progress (a narrow spread), typically while working through old supply at resistance.
ABS.pro: Professionals are absorbing the stock offered by earlier, trapped buyers; the heavy volume is buying that soaks up the selling.
ABS.next: Look for the price to hold and then move through resistance on lighter volume. Repeated failure to progress after the absorption is a warning.

BC.name: Buying climax
BC.what: A wide up bar into new highs after a rise, on ultra-high volume, closing off its high.
BC.pro: The crowd is buying on good news while professionals sell into the rush; the close off the high shows supply meeting the buying.
BC.next: Expect weakness: no-demand up bars and upthrusts confirm distribution. A low-volume test that holds would argue for more upside first.

UT.name: Upthrust
UT.what: A bar pushed up to a new high that falls back to close on or near its low, on an average-to-wide spread.
UT.pro: Prices are marked up to catch stops and lure buyers, then professionals sell into it; the close on the low shows supply.
UT.next: With weakness in the background expect lower prices, confirmed by no-demand up bars. With strength in the background it is likely to be tested or may be false.

PUT.name: Pseudo-upthrust
PUT.what: A down bar closing on its low straight after a heavy-volume up bar.
PUT.pro: The heavy buying on the prior bar met supply and the market gave it back: an upthrust spread over two bars.
PUT.next: Weak if the next up bars show no demand; a low-volume test would neutralise it. Treat it lightly.
PUT.ref: Desk-defined (not found in MTM, Holmes or WTW); weight kept low

ND.name: No demand
ND.what: A narrow up bar on volume lower than each of the two previous bars.
ND.pro: Professional money isn't interested in higher prices.
ND.next: Look for weakness to follow if the next bar closes lower; a bullish read needs a test or no supply. Inside an uptrend it is often just a pause; with weakness in the background it matters.
ND.ref: MTM p.153; Holmes p.76-84; WTW v1 p.53

EORM.name: End of a rising market
EORM.what: A narrow up bar at new highs after a rise, on ultra-high volume.
EORM.pro: Huge volume with a narrow spread means professionals are selling into the buying and capping the price; if they were buying, the spread would widen.
EORM.next: Expect weakness to follow: no demand and upthrusts. The market can drift sideways for a while before it falls.
EORM.ref: MTM p.149; Holmes p.40-41; WTW v2 p.6, p.8

ETF.name: Effort to fall
ETF.what: A wide down bar closing near its low on increased volume.
ETF.pro: Genuine selling effort: supply is in control on this bar.
ETF.next: Weak unless the next bars show stopping volume or a test. Low-volume up bars after it confirm the weakness.

FT.name: Possible failed test
FT.what: The test shape (a dip under the prior low that closes high) but on high volume.
FT.pro: The mark-down meant to test found sellers instead: supply is still present.
FT.next: Expect more testing or lower prices. A later low-volume test that holds would repair it.

SQ.name: Squat bar
SQ.what: A narrow bar on high volume: big effort, little result.
SQ.pro: Buyers and sellers are meeting head-on and someone is absorbing the other side.
SQ.next: Read it by the background: after a fall it often hints at buying (absorption), after a rise at selling. The next bar's direction shows who won.
SQ.ref: MTM p.39 (effort versus result); 'squat' is a desk label, not a named sign in the library books

NE.name: No effort (ease of movement)
NE.what: A wide-spread bar on low volume.
NE.pro: Price moved a long way on little volume: there was no professional resistance on that side, or no real interest.
NE.next: A wide up bar on low volume is suspect (no demand behind it); a wide down bar on low volume shows little selling pressure. The next bars decide.
NE.ref: MTM p.39 (effort versus result); desk glyph

abs.rule: ▲ absorption: high volume (over 1.5x the 20-bar average) on a narrow spread (under 0.7x).

ne.rule: ○ no effort: low volume (under 0.7x the 20-bar average) on a wide spread (over 1.3x).

ctx.up_sow: uptrend with weakness in the background
ctx.down_sos: downtrend with strength in the background

seq.W1: A buying climax, then supply hitting the market, then no demand: distribution is under way.
seq.W2: Supply came in twice and then buyers vanished: the rally is running out of demand.
seq.W3: Hidden selling, more supply, then no demand: professionals are quietly distributing.
seq.W4: No demand, an upthrust, and no demand again: buyers keep failing at the highs.
seq.W5: End of a rising market, an upthrust, then no demand: the top is being formed.
seq.W6: Climactic action, a failed test, then an upthrust after weakness: supply is in control.
seq.W7: An effort to rise was reversed, then an upthrust and no demand: buyers are spent.
seq.W8: A top reversal, an upthrust, then no demand: weakness confirmed at the high.
seq.W9: Supply overcame demand, an upthrust followed, then no demand: sellers in control.
seq.W10: End of a rising market followed by two no-demand bars: no professional buying left.
seq.S1: Demand overcame supply, then a test or no supply, then no supply: the selling is drying up.
seq.S2: Climactic selling met stopping volume, then a quiet test: professionals have absorbed the supply.
seq.S3: A bottom reversal, a test, then no supply: the low is being confirmed.
seq.S4: Climactic action or a shakeout, a quiet test, then no supply: the selling has been absorbed and dried up.
seq.S5: A two-bar reversal followed by no supply: little stock left for sale.
seq.S6: A shakeout, a test of the supply it hit, then no supply: weak holders are gone.
seq.S7: Bag holding, a test of the breakout, then a test in a rising market: strong hands in control.
seq.S8: Professional buying, a basic test, then no supply: the floor is holding.
seq.S9: A selling climax, a test or no supply, then demand overcoming supply: buyers are taking over.
seq.S10: A two-bar reversal from new lows followed by two no-supply bars: selling pressure has gone.
